title: U.S. House · Texas's 15th District
area: South Texas's Rio Grande Valley, including parts of Hidalgo and surrounding counties around Edinburg and McAllen.

context.text: Incumbent Republican Monica De La Cruz won her primary unopposed. Bobby Pulido, a Tejano musician and small-business owner, defeated Ada Cuellar in the Democratic primary, 67.5%-32.5%. Texas's 2025 redistricting changed roughly 80% of the district's territory from the version De La Cruz has represented since 2023; as of late September 2026, election forecasters rated the general election from Lean Republican (Cook Political Report, Decision Desk) to Tilt Republican (Inside Elections) to Toss-up (Sabato's Crystal Ball). As of June 30, 2026, De La Cruz had raised $5.27 million to Pulido's $2.96 million.

candidates.name: Monica De La Cruz
candidates.ballotNote: Won the March 3, 2026 Republican primary unopposed

summary.text: Monica De La Cruz is the Republican incumbent seeking re-election in Texas's 15th District, running in a district reshaped by 2025 redistricting so that about 80% of its territory is new to her. A former insurance agency owner, she serves on the House Agriculture and Financial Services committees and says she has passed five pieces of legislation, including a fentanyl-trafficking bill.

background.text: Born in Brownsville, Texas, in 1974; earned a bachelor's degree in business administration from the University of Texas at San Antonio in 1997.
Career experience includes owning a business and working as an insurance agent before being first elected to the House in 2022.

priorities.text: Border security, described by her campaign as a central focus of her time in office.
South Texas agriculture and water: created the South Texas Water Working Group and says she is pressing the Mexican government to meet water-treaty obligations to the region.

record.text: Serves on the Committee on Agriculture as Vice Chair of its Subcommittee on Nutrition and Foreign Agriculture, and on its Subcommittee on General Farm Commodities, Risk Management, and Credit, for the 119th Congress (2025-2026).
Serves as Vice Chair of the Committee on Financial Services for the 119th Congress.

Her campaign says she secured passage of five pieces of legislation during her time in office, including a bill targeting fentanyl trafficking that her campaign describes as the first bill from her community signed into law in nearly 20 years.

candidates.name: Bobby Pulido
candidates.ballotNote: Won the March 3, 2026 Democratic primary, 67.5%-32.5%, over Ada Cuellar

summary.text: Bobby Pulido is the Democratic nominee challenging incumbent Monica De La Cruz in Texas's 15th District. A lifelong South Texan, small-business owner, father of four and Tejano recording artist from Edinburg, he is campaigning on affordability, water infrastructure and public education.

background.text: Born and raised in Edinburg, Texas; studied political science at St. Mary's University before building a career as a Tejano music artist.
Has run small businesses in South Texas in addition to his music career.

priorities.text: Public education: opposes private-school voucher programs and wants higher teacher pay and reduced classroom overcrowding.
Water infrastructure: supports investment in desalination and modern irrigation to address the Rio Grande Valley's water shortage, and wants Mexico held to its water-treaty obligations.
Affordability, including lowering costs for families and small businesses.

positions.summary: Says he opposes voucher programs that he says drain money from public classrooms and send it to private schools.
